_about: Shared, editable text and option tables used by every ship and site. Archetype files can add their own entries.

condition_notes.Scrap: Barely held together; most systems are stripped or failing.
condition_notes.Derelict: Long abandoned. Dust, ice and decay; little works without repair.
condition_notes.Disrepair: Worn out and neglected. Systems fail without warning.
condition_notes.Average: Ordinary working order, worn but serviceable.
condition_notes.Cluttered: Crammed with crates, gear and personal junk. Cover everywhere, movement slow.
condition_notes.Sleeper: Quiet and tidy on the surface; much of it is shut down or on standby.
condition_notes.Well Maintained: Clean, serviced and orderly. Someone cares about this place.
condition_notes.Top of the Line: Pristine and state of the art. The company spared no expense.

peculiarities.name: Flickering lights
peculiarities.text: Lighting stutters in the lower corridors. Hard to tell what moves in the dark.

peculiarities.name: Phantom alarms
peculiarities.text: A fire alarm sounds without cause every few hours; everyone has stopped reacting to it.

peculiarities.name: Unreliable lifts
peculiarities.text: Lifts stall between decks about one trip in six.

peculiarities.name: Company store debt
peculiarities.text: Nearly every resident owes the company; loyalty is purchased, not freely given.

peculiarities.name: Missing logs
peculiarities.text: Maintenance logs for one entire week have been wiped.

peculiarities.name: Sticky doors
peculiarities.text: Several doors jam half-open and need a hard shove.

peculiarities.name: Excellent water
peculiarities.text: The water recyclers are unusually good; supplies last far longer than expected.

peculiarities.name: Hidden stash
peculiarities.text: A previous occupant left a sealed locker of useful equipment behind a service panel.

peculiarities.name: Redundant power
peculiarities.text: A forgotten backup generator can restore power to one zone.

peculiarities.name: Friendly foreman
peculiarities.text: A senior worker quietly sympathises with outsiders and can bend the rules once.

peculiarities.name: Strong hull
peculiarities.text: Reinforced structure; breaches are rare and slow.

peculiarities.name: Good coffee
peculiarities.text: The mess serves the best coffee on the frontier. Morale is surprisingly high.

Break In: The party must reach {zone:secure} unseen and copy what is stored there before the next shift change.
Someone hired the party to get into {zone:restricted} and leave no trace of the visit.
Break Out: A contact is held in {zone:secure}. The party has until the next resupply flight to get them out.
An alarm sealed the party in near {zone:public}; they must reach a way out through {zone:staff}.
Rescue: A distress call came from {zone:staff}. Survivors may still be alive, and they are not alone.
A survey team failed to report in. Their last position was {zone:any}.
Salvage: The company wrote this place off. Anything left in {zone:any} belongs to whoever hauls it out first.
A rival crew has already stripped half the complex. The party races them to {zone:restricted}.
Investigate: Production stopped without explanation. Records point to {zone:restricted}.
Three workers died the same night in {zone:staff}. The official report says accident.
Defend: Something is coming. The party must hold {zone:public} until the transport can lift off.
The facility is under attack and the only working comms are in {zone:staff}.
Sabotage: The company is hiding something in {zone:restricted}. Destroy it before it ships.
Shut down {zone:any} without raising the alarm and without hurting the crew.
Cover-up: Corporate wants every trace removed from {zone:restricted}, including the witnesses.
An accident in {zone:staff} must look like it never happened.
Escape: Containment failed. The only route to the surface runs through {zone:any}.
Quarantine seals drop in minutes. The party is on the wrong side.
Abandoned Facility: No one has answered hails for months. The lights are still on in {zone:any}.
The facility looks untouched, yet every person is gone. Something stayed behind.

notes: Lighting, climate and noise can change the mood of a room without changing a single wall.
Doors marked as locked can be opened with the matching access level; secure zones should need more than a keycard.
Treat unmarked corridors as the shortest routes between numbered rooms; use the key for what is inside.
Use the player version of the map at the table and keep the GM version, with secrets and threat markers, behind the screen.

breathable.label: Breathable surface
breathable.note: The air is breathable, if cold and thin in places.

hostile.label: Hostile atmosphere
hostile.note: The air outside is toxic or corrosive. Everything seals; suits are required outdoors.

vacuum.label: Vacuum
vacuum.note: No atmosphere outside. Every exterior door is an airlock.

underground.label: Underground
underground.note: Only a small structure is visible at the surface; the rest is carved into rock.

orbital.label: Orbital or underwater / ice
orbital.note: Outside is hard vacuum or deep water or ice; treat every exterior door as an airlock.

threat.note: Threat markers are generic. Describe the creature, intruder or hazard however your game needs.

secrets: Hidden room behind a false wall
Secret lab behind a vending alcove

closers: Few outsiders see more than the front desk.
Nothing here is quite what the company records claim.
Supplies arrive late and questions are not welcome.
The crew keeps to routine and avoids certain rooms.

bridge: The nerve centre: consoles, a command chair and a wall of status displays.
Command stations ring a central holo-table; the screens never fully go dark.
engineering: Machinery hums behind guard rails; gauges, pipes and warning placards everywhere.
A noisy, hot space of coolant lines, spare parts and tool racks.
power: Power cabling thicker than a wrist runs from the main buses into the walls.
fuel: Tank housings and transfer lines; the air smells faintly of hydrocarbon.
cargo: Racks, crates and cargo cradles under strapping nets.
Stacked containers, loader machinery and manifest terminals.
hangar: A high bay with docking cradles, tie-downs and a fuel cart left where it was parked.
vehicle_bay: Vehicle racks, charging cables and a workbench scattered with parts.
docking: Docking collars and boarding tubes; scuffed decals mark who last parked here.
weapons: Gun mounts and ammunition feeds; every surface is scuffed from handling.
armory: Locked racks, a signed-out register and a heavy door that sticks when it's closed.
staterooms: Narrow cabins with bunks, lockers and personal belongings.
Rows of cramped cabins off a short central corridor.
crew_quarters: Personal effects, bunks and a shared fresher at the end of the row.
barracks: Rows of bunks and footlockers, kept neat out of habit.
galley: A galley and mess: steel counters, a long table, the smell of reheated food.
medical: Beds, scanners and a supply cabinet that is never quite full.
A clinic with exam bays, a surgery and a small pharmacy.
lab: Benches, sample cabinets and analyzers; some work is still under cloth.
A laboratory: fume hoods, centrifuges and a wall of sealed specimen drawers.
hydroponics: Racks of growing plants under purple light; the air is humid and green.
recreation: A lounge with worn seating, a bar and a games table.
A common area where people trade rumours and spend wages.
concourse: A busy concourse with benches, signage and vending alcoves.
passenger: Passenger accommodation, better kept than the crew's.
security: A security station with monitors, a weapons locker and holding benches.
brig: Cells with fixed bunks and a guard desk with a clear view.
office: Desks, terminals and filing cabinets; paper trails beat digital ones here.
workshop: Benches, tool racks and half-finished repairs.
waste: Compactors, sorting bins and an incinerator with a heavy, scorched door.
water: Tanks, filters and pumps; the sound of running water echoes.
refinery: Processing machinery and vats; everything is stained and warm.
sensors: Sensor consoles and antenna feeds; operators sit hunched over scopes.
comms: Comm racks, a relay console and a tangle of patch cables.
escape: Escape pod bays with alarm placards and sealed hatches.
lowberth: Rows of sleeper pods, frosted and humming softly.
airlock: An airlock chamber with suit lockers and a pressure gauge.
vertical: Lifts, stairs and shaft access; the one place everyone passes through.
interstitial: Maintenance crawlspace, pipes and cable runs.
multipurpose: A mix of rooms: offices, stores and cabins under one roof.
_default: A working space; its purpose is clear from the equipment.
